title: Iframe fallback
description: Wraps any wp-admin URL inside the workspace. Chrome hidden via injected CSS.

documentation.purpose: Renders any wp-admin URL inside an iframe with the default wp-admin shell hidden via injected CSS. Absolute URLs pass through; relative URLs resolve under `window.wpAdminWorkspaces.adminUrl`. The base chrome-hide CSS targets adminmenu / adminbar / footer / wpcontent margin — the wp-admin shell common to every admin page. `config.hideEditorChrome: true` additionally strips the block editor's own sidebar / site-hub / header / canvas container (only preview/embed surfaces should opt in; see #253). The workspace's escape hatch: any wp-admin screen without a native v2 port can be surfaced through this app without writing custom React.

states.renders: Centered Spinner overlaid on the iframe element.
Full-bleed iframe with chrome hidden (best-effort — cross-origin iframes silently skip the injection).

interactions.effect: Set `isLoading=false`; attempt to inject the wp-admin shell-hide CSS into `event.target.contentDocument` (plus the editor-chrome selectors when `config.hideEditorChrome`). Cross-origin iframes throw and we silently swallow.

a11y.focus-management: Iframe owns its own focus tree; the workspace does not trap.

constraints.note: Base chrome-hide selectors target wp-admin's shell class names (`#adminmenuwrap`, `#wpadminbar`, `#wpcontent`). The fragile edit-site selectors (`.edit-site-layout__sidebar*`, `.edit-site-site-hub`, `.edit-site-layout__header-container`, canvas container) are opt-in via `config.hideEditorChrome` — only injected for preview/embed surfaces. Rev with each WordPress release; the Style Book canvas in edit-site has historically been the most fragile.

Cross-origin iframes can't have CSS injected (DOM access throws). We swallow the exception silently — the iframe still loads, but with wp-admin chrome visible. Production sites that embed cross-origin URLs accept this trade-off.
Schema allows additional properties on `config` because adapters (SiteEditorApp, custom apps that delegate to IframeApp) may carry extra fields. The app itself only reads `url`.

The iframe's `title` attribute is set to `app.title` (static, from the manifest). The embedded page's `<title>` does not propagate up — same-origin would technically allow reading it on load, but cross-origin would silently fail, and the inconsistency outweighs the value.

Manifest declares `role: "main"` but this app is mounted in any region — `content`, `detail`, a windowed region under `core:desktop`, etc. The engine template's region role (applied to the region wrapper by the kernel) wins; the manifest role is documentation only and reflects the most common mount target. Authors mounting this app outside a `main`-shaped region should not expect the landmark to follow.

On the `core:desktop` engine, `core:desktop-iframe` is the sibling app that wraps any wp-admin URL with `?wp_admin_workspaces_chromeless=1`. That triggers a PHP-side chromeless bridge (`includes/engines/core-desktop/chromeless-bridge.php`) attaching a 14-subsystem JS payload — error/fetch/XHR wraps, navigation interception, auth recovery, command-palette harvest (stub). This iframe-fallback app is the underlying primitive; `core:desktop-iframe` extends it with a parent-side `postMessage` listener routing `focus-request` / `admin-link` / `external-link` events. A rebuild of this app in a non-default engine should be aware of the bridge contract so a desktop-style engine port can wire its parent-side listener the same way.
